html:
The Battle of Bicocca was fought on 27 April 1522 in the park of Bicocca, a country house just north of Milan in northern Italy. An army of the emperor Charles V and the pope, led by Prospero Colonna, beat a French and Venetian army under the Viscount of Lautrec.

France and the emperor were fighting over the Duchy of Milan in the Italian Wars. Lautrec's best troops were Swiss pikemen, hired soldiers who had not been paid. They told him to fight at once or they would go home. So he had to attack Colonna in a position chosen for defence: a sunken road in front of an earth bank, lined with cannon and Spanish arquebusiers standing four deep. The Swiss marched straight at it without waiting for the French guns. They were shot down in the road and could not climb the bank. About 3,000 died in half an hour.

The Swiss went home, and their pike squares never again attacked with the old confidence. Guns behind earthworks had beaten the best infantry in Europe, as at Cerignola. France lost Milan. In Spanish, a bicoca came to mean an easy prize.
